Source.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/6] adolescents and their parent(s) were administered the Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Aged Children, Epidemiological Version (K-SADS-E; Orvaschel & Puig-Antich, 1986). The K-SADS-E is a semi-structured diagnostic interview, in which both a parent, typically the mother, and the adolescent are interviewed separately regarding the teenager's psychiatric symptoms. On the basis of information from both, the examiner makes a 'summary' clinical judgment as to the presence or absence of the symptoms. [/page/6/Text/5] The CES-D (Radloff, 1977) is a 20-item self-report measure of depressive symptoms. [/page/7/Text/2] In addition to the self-report depression scales, adolescents were asked to complete instruments which had been selected to assess psychosocial constructs known to be associated with depression in individuals: depressogenic cognitions, pleasant events, anxiety, and social skills. These, along with conflict-resolution skills were targeted in the CWD-A course and measured pre and posttreatment. Depressogenic cognitions were measured by abbreviated versions of the Subjective Probability Questionnaire (SPQ; Mufioz & Lewinsohn, 1976), [...] the Dysfunctional Attitude Scale (DAS; Weissman & Beck, 1978) [...] and the Personal Beliefs Inventory (PBI; Mufioz & Lewinsohn, 1976) [...]. Pleasant events were measured by the Pleasant Events Schedule (PES; Mac-Phillamy & Lewinsohn, 1982) [...]. State anxiety was measured by an abbreviation of the Spielberger State Anxiety Questionnaire (SAQ; Spielberger, 1979), [...]. Conflict resolution was measured by the Issues Checklist (IC; Robin & Weiss, 1980)
